original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

actual_scope: On the PR2322 T74 words: how much paid recursive mass is pure end-of-call restoration (FULL-cleanup end climbs), what do zero buffers cost under the PR2374 outer, and what is each additional cold-restored (hyperplane-ended) helper worth in the width-aware LP ceiling?
scope_change_reason: Drawn on the recursive-interfaces track (seed 55: eliminate boundary or restoration work with a complete cost recurrence). Its cards (centre sharing, coverage law, connectors, QQ16) are saturated; the concrete restoration item on the live T74 line is the end-climb restoration of FULL-cleanup helpers, whose removal is a changed local cleanup contract, so it is filed under the helper-inventory/local-interface card.
bottleneck_link: End-of-call restoration climbs are 9.8% of the local paid mass of the PR2322 words; each additional cold-restored helper is worth up to +1.46e-6 in the LP ceiling, far above the owner-fill and handoff increments of the current T74 line, and zero buffers are free in kappa under the PR2374 outer.
stop_rule: Stop after the census (checked independently), the cost-context facts from pinned PR2374 files, and LP prices per class, per bulk class and ideal; no commutation search or construction this session.
evidence: restoration_prices.py: 356 FULL-cleanup helpers pay end climbs {1:249,2:42,3:64} = 525 rank units/call; 78 cold-restored pay none; kappa = C - 1/F - B (F=1e3046, B=1e-3022); physical 66826 -> 67181 <= 112178; NZ 433 <= R 434; one conversion +5.77e-7 / +1.04e-6 / +1.46e-6; ideal all 355 LP ceiling 0.0018806 (+10.8%). Independent subagent recount agrees on all census numbers.

open_questions.question: Which of the 355 FULL-cleanup helpers admit an earlier cleanup under an exact (not merely sufficient) commutation test?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Each conversion is worth +5.8e-7 to +1.46e-6 in the LP ceiling; the existing hyperplane-ended helpers come from PR601's sufficient test.
open_questions.first_step: For each helper compute the maximal commuting suffix of gates with its cleanup gates exactly over the dyadic scalars, starting with the 64 end-climb-3 helpers.
open_questions.blocked_by: Cleanup semantics of the T74 words (inverse-reverse cleanup, buffers) must be modelled exactly; not done here.

open_questions.question: Can a PR604-style cold tail restore one end-climb-3 helper on the PR2322 words, and at what full price?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Cold tails add gates whose frames may force other climbs; only an actual word recount prices them.
open_questions.first_step: Apply PR604's tail constructor to one helper and recount with this package's recount.
open_questions.blocked_by: PR604's constructor targets an older word family; porting is needed.
